protocol.instrument_name: Enhanced Access Community Pharmacy Pilot - Application Information Pack
protocol.effective_date: September 2026 (cover page; version control table: 1.0 August 2026 First version, 1.1 September 2026 Revised version, updated QSPP requirements)
protocol.legal_basis: Not stated in this document; no Act, regulation, schedule provision or SASA is cited. The document concerns the application process for pharmacy owners and pharmacists seeking to participate in the Enhanced Access Community Pharmacy Pilot (EACPP) in WA only.
protocol.supervision_model: Not stated in this document; participation is conditional on the pharmacist adhering to 'the rules and conditions set out in the EACPP Handbook, including to provide services in accordance with the relevant EACPP clinical practice guideline or protocol issued by the department' and on being informed by the department of eligibility before commencing delivery of EACPP services (p.8).
protocol.scope_summary: SUPPORTING / ADMINISTRATIVE DOCUMENT, NOT A CLINICAL PRESCRIBING PROTOCOL: the application information pack for the WA EACPP (September 2026). It covers overview and eligibility (p.3), mandatory pharmacist participation requirements (pp.3-4), mandatory pharmacy participation requirements (pp.4-5), consultation room requirements and Table 1 (pp.5-6), the application process (pp.6-7), pharmacist/pharmacy application form details and declarations (pp.7-9), notification of change in details (p.9) and version control (p.10). It contains administrative participation requirements only - no patient eligibility criteria, no medicines, no doses, no assessment pathway and no clinical red flags; the administrative requirements are captured as eligibility criteria with provenance.

inclusion.text: Community pharmacies located in WA, and pharmacists who are employed at a community pharmacy located in WA, are eligible to participate once they have met the participation requirements and have been informed by the Department of Health (the department) of their eligibility to participate in the EACPP.
The Requirements for participating pharmacists and Requirements for participating pharmacies are mandatory requirements to participate in the EACPP.
The pharmacist must hold general registration with the Pharmacy Board of Australia, with no conditions on practice.
The pharmacist must hold appropriate professional indemnity insurance to cover the services provided as part of the EACPP.
The pharmacist must hold, for the duration of the EACPP, certification for First Aid and CPR.

The pharmacist must demonstrate successful completion of an approved training program that covers the knowledge and skills required to deliver EACPP services. An approved training program must be: a. Accredited by the Australian Pharmacy Council (APC) in accordance with the Accreditation Standards for Pharmacist Prescriber education programs. b. Recognised as an Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) Level 8 Graduate Certificate. c. Assessed and approved by the department and published on the EACPP website.

The pharmacist must agree to the rules and conditions set out in the EACPP Handbook, including: a. Providing services in accordance with the relevant EACPP Clinical Practice Guideline or Protocol at a participating pharmacy. b. Using an approved EACPP Clinical Information System to record clinical consultations and collect data for the evaluation of the EACPP. c. Participation in other activities that are required to enable quality and safety monitoring and evaluation of the EACPP. [item 5 begins on page 3; sub-items a-c are printed on page 4]
The pharmacist must agree to their full name and Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency registration number appearing in the EACPP participating pharmacist database.

The pharmacy be accredited against or actively progressing towards accreditation against the AS85000:2024 Australian Community Pharmacy Standard through an approved pharmacy or primary care accreditation program, such as the Quality and Safety Pharmacy Program (QSPP). Participating pharmacies are to hold or actively progress towards QSPP accreditation that includes Full Scope of Practice certification (or equivalent): Pharmacies currently holding Quality Care Pharmacy Program (QCPP) accreditation will transition to QSPP on 1 October 2026: QSPP has advised that these pharmacies that wish to be considered for EACPP must apply for a QSPP Expansion of Service, Full Scope of Practice assessment; these pharmacies must submit the QSPP Accreditation Certificate that includes Full Scope of Practice certification as part of their EACPP application; QSPP has advised that where a QSPP accredited pharmacy is found to have been offering or advertising a service which is not within the service level for which they are QSPP accredited, a sanction may be issued by QSPP; please refer to the QSPP Knowledge Hub (member log-in required) for more information. Pharmacies with no current accreditation must attain a QSPP Accreditation Certificate that includes Full Scope of Practice certification (or equivalent) by 30 June 2027.
The pharmacy owner must demonstrate compliance with appropriate infrastructure requirements as set out in the EACPP Handbook.
The pharmacy must have access to an approved EACPP Clinical Information System software to record clinical consultations and collect data for the evaluation of the EACPP.
The pharmacy owner must hold, for the duration of the EACPP, professional indemnity insurance that explicitly covers the pharmacy's involvement in the EACPP.
The pharmacy owner must provide access for participating pharmacists to the required resources and reference materials.
The pharmacy owner must provide access for participating pharmacists to the current online version of the Therapeutic Guidelines.
The pharmacy owner must agree to their pharmacy information appearing on the EACPP participating pharmacy premises database and Find a Pharmacy website.

Pilot services must be delivered in a private consultation room for patient privacy and to ensure confidential conversations and patient examinations can be conducted. These requirements are for a consultation area that: Allows for confidential sit-down consultations between the participating pharmacist and patient and/or substitute decision maker; Allows the participating pharmacist and patient and/or substitute decision maker to talk at normal speaking volumes without being overheard by others; Is not within the dispensary.

Table 1: Pilot service room requirements [table printed across pages 5-6] - Privacy: the room is fully enclosed and ensures auditory privacy so the patient and the pharmacist can talk at normal speaking volumes without being overheard by any other person; entry to and exit from the consultation room must avoid any area where a patient has access to any scheduled medicines, including walking through or near stock in the dispensary; the room must be clearly identified as a private consultation room; entry to the room must be restricted so that consultations are not interrupted by customers/staff. Space: sufficient floor area clear of equipment and furniture to accommodate the pharmacist, the patient and a carer, documentation, and consumables; adequate space to manoeuvre and sufficient space for the patient to lie down, and for the staff to safely perform resuscitation procedures; the room must be used for pharmacy services and consultations only and must not be used as a dispensary, storeroom, staff room, or Dose Administration Aids filling room. Furniture, general equipment, and ambience: a desk and office chair for the pharmacist with a computer and appropriate space to conduct the consultation; adequate and functional seating for the patient and a carer with minimum capacity of 150 kg; an examination table or all-purpose fully reclinable bed-chair; a computer with an approved clinical information system available and accessible during the consultation; computer screens located so they don't block patient interactions but keep private information out of sight; access to a printer, or located near one, to provide printed documentation to patients when required; a height-measurement device and a scale; lockable storage if storing clinical equipment, medicines, and consumables in the room (medicines must not be clearly visible to prevent unauthorised access); sufficient bench space with an impervious surface; recommended handwashing facilities in the room (if handwashing facilities are not in the room, hand sanitisation facilities in the room and ready access to handwashing facilities); flooring that is easy to clean; sufficient lighting to effectively examine the patient and conduct the consultation; the consultation room maintained at a comfortable ambient temperature. Accessibility: easy access for patients with disability who are accompanied by a family member or a carer. Emergency equipment: up to date first-aid kit and anaphylaxis kit; access within the premises to an Automated External Defibrillator is preferred, but not mandatory. Other safety features: unhindered access for emergency staff to attend and perform resuscitation procedures; consider doors that open outwards or sliding doors to ensure that outside emergency access cannot be blocked from inside the room; a medical waste and sharps container that meets Australian standards stored in a safe location; safe location of cables, power cords, and power points. The EACPP accepts the Quality and Safety Pharmacy Program (QSPP) Level 3 accreditation (or equivalent) as evidence that these consultation room requirements have been met.

To participate in the EACPP, community pharmacists and community pharmacy owners (or pharmacist with overall responsibility) must apply and be informed by the department of their eligibility to participate. Pharmacists are required to complete the Pharmacist Application Form indicating they have met the requirements to participate. Pharmacy owners (or pharmacist with overall responsibility) are required to complete the Pharmacy Application Form on behalf of their pharmacy and provide declarations in relation to the readiness of the pharmacy to provide pilot services.

Pharmacist declaration of the conditions for participation: I understand that in order to participate in the EACPP: a. I must meet the pharmacist participation requirements. b. I must be informed by the department of my eligibility to participate in the EACPP, prior to commencing the delivery of EACPP services. c. I must adhere to the rules and conditions set out in the EACPP Handbook, including to provide services in accordance with the relevant EACPP clinical practice guideline or protocol issued by the department. d. I must continue to meet the requirements for participating pharmacists for the duration of my participation in the EACPP. e. I must only deliver EACPP services at a participating pharmacy, which must continue to meet all pharmacy requirements for the duration of its participation in the EACPP. [declaration 3 printed across pages 7-8]

Pharmacy owner (or pharmacist with overall responsibility) declaration of the conditions for participation: I understand that in order to participate in the EACPP: a. Both my pharmacy and the participating pharmacist/s providing EACPP services at my pharmacy must meet the participation requirements. b. Both my pharmacy and the participating pharmacist/s providing EACPP services at my pharmacy must be informed by the department of our eligibility to participate in the EACPP, prior to commencing the delivery of EACPP services. c. My participating pharmacist/s and I must adhere to the rules and conditions set out in the EACPP Handbook, including to provide services in accordance with the relevant EACPP clinical practice guideline or protocol issued by the department. d. My pharmacy must continue to meet the requirements of participating pharmacies for the duration of participation in the EACPP. e. My participating pharmacist/s must continue to meet the pharmacist requirements for the duration of their participation in the EACPP, at my pharmacy.
I will notify the department within 5 business days if there are any changes to my name, contact, Ahpra registration details, or ability to meet any of the pharmacist participation requirements.
I will notify the department within 5 business days if I become aware of any investigation by a regulatory authority relating to my practice as a pharmacist.

I will notify the department within 5 business days if there are any changes to the business name, contact details for the pharmacy, a change in the EACPP services provided by the pharmacy named in this application form, or ability to meet any of the pharmacy participation requirements.

Pharmacists are required to notify the Pilot Coordination Team at DOH.EACPP@health.wa.gov.au if any of the following details of the participating pharmacist change: the name of the pharmacist; the contact details of the pharmacist; the Ahpra registration details or any change in conditions on the registration; criminal history; no longer meet any of the pharmacist participation requirements; the pharmacist wishes to stop providing services and withdraw from the EACPP.

Pharmacy owners (or pharmacist with overall responsibility) are required to notify the Pilot Coordination Team at DOH.EACPP@health.wa.gov.au if any of the following details for a participating pharmacy change: the contact details for the pharmacy owner (or pharmacist with overall responsibility); the address of the pharmacy; contact details for the pharmacy; pharmacy website or consultation booking details; no longer meet any of the pharmacy participation requirements; the pharmacy premises wishes to stop providing services and withdraw from the EACPP.

exclusion.text: I understand that this application only relates to EACPP in WA, and it does not extend to pharmacist prescribing in other states and territories. [pharmacist declaration 5, page 8; the same declaration appears as pharmacy declaration 6 on page 9]
I understand that giving false or misleading information may result in removal from EACPP participation.

red_flags.trigger_text: I understand that giving false or misleading information may result in removal from EACPP participation. [pharmacist declaration 8, page 8; pharmacy declaration 8, page 9]

no longer meet any of the pharmacist participation requirements [must be notified to the Pilot Coordination Team at DOH.EACPP@health.wa.gov.au; the declarations also require notification to the department within 5 business days if the pharmacist's ability to meet any of the pharmacist participation requirements changes]

no longer meet any of the pharmacy participation requirements [must be notified to the Pilot Coordination Team at DOH.EACPP@health.wa.gov.au; the declarations also require notification to the department within 5 business days if the pharmacy's ability to meet any of the pharmacy participation requirements changes]

review_followup.when: For the duration of a pharmacist's and pharmacy's participation in the EACPP
review_followup.what: Compliance checks will also occur to ensure information that is provided through the application forms remains current for the duration of a pharmacist's and pharmacy's participation in the EACPP; the department will undertake checks against the information provided in the application forms, including verification with education providers regarding training courses completed.

conditions: The pharmacist must notify the department within 5 business days of any changes to name, contact, Ahpra registration details, or ability to meet any of the pharmacist participation requirements (pharmacist declaration 6, p.8), and within 5 business days of becoming aware of any investigation by a regulatory authority relating to their practice as a pharmacist (pharmacist declaration 7, p.8).

Pharmacists are required to notify the Pilot Coordination Team at DOH.EACPP@health.wa.gov.au if any listed pharmacist details change: name; contact details; Ahpra registration details or any change in conditions on the registration; criminal history; no longer meeting any of the pharmacist participation requirements; wishing to stop providing services and withdraw from the EACPP (p.9).

Pharmacy owners (or pharmacist with overall responsibility) must notify the department within 5 business days of any changes to business name, pharmacy contact details, EACPP services provided by the pharmacy, or ability to meet any of the pharmacy participation requirements (pharmacy declaration 7, p.9), and must notify the Pilot Coordination Team at DOH.EACPP@health.wa.gov.au if any listed pharmacy details change: contact details for the pharmacy owner; address of the pharmacy; contact details for the pharmacy; pharmacy website or consultation booking details; no longer meeting any of the pharmacy participation requirements; wishing to stop providing services and withdraw from the EACPP (p.9).

open_questions.topic: This is an administrative application information pack, not a clinical prescribing protocol
open_questions.observed: The document is the 'Application Information Pack' (September 2026) for the Enhanced Access Community Pharmacy Pilot. It contains Overview, Eligibility, Pilot requirements, Requirements for participating pharmacists/pharmacies, Consultation room requirements, Application process, Application Form requirements, Declarations, Notification of change in details and Version control. It has no patient inclusion/exclusion criteria, no medicines or doses, no diagnosis/assessment pathway and no clinical referral triggers.
open_questions.why_unclear: Per the extraction spec's NON-PROTOCOL DOCUMENTS rule, clinical arrays (diagnosis_pathways, treatments) are left empty rather than fabricated; the administrative requirements are captured as eligibility criteria with provenance.

open_questions.topic: Red flags present are administrative consequence triggers, not clinical escalation triggers
open_questions.observed: The only escalation/consequence wording in the document is administrative: 'giving false or misleading information may result in removal from EACPP participation' (p.8) and 'no longer meet any of the pharmacist/pharmacy participation requirements' requiring notification (p.9). There is no clinical referral, urgency or emergency wording anywhere in the 11 pages.
open_questions.why_unclear: RF-1 to RF-3 are captured with their exact wording as NOT_ELIGIBLE consequences; no clinical red flag exists to extract, so any expectation of clinical triggers is not met by this document type.

open_questions.observed: The only use of the word 'refer' is administrative: 'Please refer to the QSPP Knowledge Hub (member log-in required) for more information' (p.4). No patient referral destination, urgency tier or emergency pathway appears.
open_questions.why_unclear: referral.routine/urgent/emergency are empty because the document genuinely contains no referral content; provenance points to the Application process section for the block.

open_questions.observed: Eligibility on page 3 is expressed as 'WA community pharmacies and pharmacists working within these pharmacies may apply to participate' plus the participation requirements; no patient or practitioner age limit is printed anywhere.
open_questions.why_unclear: age_bounds is null/null with provenance to the Eligibility section.

open_questions.topic: The ordered application process is administrative, not a clinical pathway
open_questions.observed: Page 6-7 process: apply via the Pharmacist Application Form and Pharmacy Application Form; provide declarations; upload documentation; the department undertakes checks against the application forms including verification with education providers; applicants must then be informed by the department of their eligibility before commencing EACPP services.
open_questions.why_unclear: This is an application workflow rather than a diagnosis/assessment pathway, so diagnosis_pathways is left empty rather than populated with a mis-typed clinical pathway.

open_questions.topic: Referenced documents are not included with this pack
open_questions.observed: The pack depends on the EACPP Handbook (rules, conditions, infrastructure requirements), the EACPP Clinical Practice Guidelines/Protocols, the list of approved EACPP Clinical Information Systems, the approved training program list published on the EACPP website, and the actual Pharmacist and Pharmacy Application Forms with their documentation upload requirements.
open_questions.why_unclear: Those instruments cannot be transcribed from this file; their content is recorded here rather than inferred.

open_questions.topic: notifiable captures departmental notification requirements, not notifiable conditions
open_questions.observed: The document requires notification to the department / Pilot Coordination Team (within 5 business days for listed changes) but is silent on notifiable conditions, GP notification or AIR notification.
open_questions.why_unclear: notifiable.required is set true only for the departmental/Pilot Coordination Team notification obligations that are explicitly printed; no public-health notification requirement exists in this document.

open_questions.topic: No legal basis or authorisation wording printed
open_questions.observed: No Act, regulation, schedule provision or SASA is cited; the document is an application information pack only, and the cover page carries the WA Health 'Classification: Official' marking.
open_questions.why_unclear: legal_basis cannot be populated from this document; the prescribing legal basis sits in the clinical practice guidelines/protocols or the Medicines and Poisons Regulations 2016 (WA), which are not reproduced here.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the QSPP/QCPP transition arrangements and accreditation deadlines are current at go-live: QCPP-accredited pharmacies transition to QSPP on 1 October 2026 and must apply for a QSPP Expansion of Service, Full Scope of Practice assessment; pharmacies with no current accreditation must attain a QSPP Accreditation Certificate including Full Scope of Practice certification (or equivalent) by 30 June 2027.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Dated, jurisdiction-specific accreditation conditions in a September 2026 pilot document (version 1.1 'updated QSPP requirements'); they must be verified against the current QSPP/department position.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the specific approved training program(s) published on the EACPP website that satisfy requirement 4 (APC-accredited, AQF Level 8 Graduate Certificate, assessed and approved by the department).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The document defines the attributes of an approved program but names no course; go-live eligibility checks need the actual approved list.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the contents of the EACPP Handbook (rules, conditions, infrastructure requirements) and the list of approved EACPP Clinical Information Systems.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Multiple mandatory requirements are defined purely by reference to documents not supplied with this pack, so they cannot be evaluated as hard checks without local confirmation.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm how consultation room compliance is evidenced: QSPP Level 3 accreditation (or equivalent) is accepted as evidence of Table 1; otherwise a completed statutory declaration of consultation-room suitability is required with the application.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The evidence route differs by accreditation status and the statutory declaration wording is not reproduced in this pack; the operating procedure must be confirmed before go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm that version 1.1 (September 2026, Revised version, updated QSPP requirements) is the current controlled version and obtain the formal effective/approval date.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The version control table prints month/year only and no approving officer; effective_date is taken from the cover page and version table.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the interpretation and ownership of the notification obligations (department vs Pilot Coordination Team at DOH.EACPP@health.wa.gov.au, and the 5-business-day timeframe, which is stated in the declarations rather than in the Notification of change in details list).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Two notification mechanisms with overlapping triggers are printed on different pages; the operative timeframe and recipient for each change type must be confirmed before the module encodes them as obligations.
